description: Executable local MinIO drill proving that one explicitly selected source object version can be copied into a separate versioned backup bucket, survive complete source-version removal and be restored into a third bucket with checksum and source-version binding intact. It is not production independent retention, TLS, credential separation, lifecycle, provider durability or coherent PostgreSQL/object recovery evidence.

requiredSteps: create separate source backup and restore buckets
select one non-latest source version explicitly
read the selected source version by VersionId
copy bytes and authoritative checksum binding into the backup bucket
record source-version digest in backup metadata
remove every source object version and delete marker
verify the source object is unavailable
read the exact backup version by VersionId
verify restored bytes checksum length metadata and independent version identifiers
write exact-source machine-readable evidence without credentials or raw provider identifiers
successCriteria: source has at least three distinct versions before loss
backup and restore buckets are versioned
selected source version is read explicitly rather than by latest
backup copy checksum equals selected source checksum
backup metadata binds the digest of the selected source version
all source versions and delete markers are removed before restore
restore reads an explicit backup VersionId
restored checksum and content length equal the selected source version
source backup and restore version identifiers are distinct
abortCriteria: ephemeral object deletion permission is absent
backup source-version binding is missing or mismatched
credential endpoint raw version identifier object key or payload would enter evidence

evidenceBoundary.note: A PASS proves only local version-addressed copy and restore across three MinIO buckets. It does not establish production object backup or satisfy OPS-P0-007 by itself.
